Beauty pass

Noah asked to make Tailspot more beautiful. Every snapshot screen was rendered. Seven design critics audited one surface each from the pixels and the code, and a skeptic per surface struck anything not visible or against a settled call. The survivors were built, then compared before and after by a fresh reviewer per surface; the regressions it caught were fixed or reverted. These are the real SwiftUI views from the test harness.

64findings proposed
49survived review
~35shipped here
7left for your call
1,897tests passing

Capture screen

Steering pill on a day sky

The pill fill goes from 55% to 75% with a hairline edge, so it stops washing out to grey slate. A pointing arrow replaces the breathing dot, so the direction reads at a glance.

The amber glow (an olive fog on a blue sky) becomes a plain drop shadow. The sentence is now prose, "Labels may be wrong. Tap to calibrate.", with the mono caps head kept.

Left for your call

These change the look enough that they should be picked from a mock, not shipped in a polish pass.

  • B612 on the reveal and share artboards. Both are drawn in SF Mono, while every other surface uses the brand's B612 Mono. Switching makes the catch moment match the rest of the app, but B612 is wider, so long names and big numbers need refitting. A visible change to the most-seen screen, so it should be your call from a mock.
  • Onboarding back chevron. Onboarding's "Back" is small grey text under the CTA. The exit rule says back is a chevron top left. The back-controls audit marked onboarding out of scope, and onboarding is App Review sensitive.
  • Challenge create sheet off Form. The create sheet uses stock Form geometry, so its radii and left edges don't match the rest of Challenges. A real rebuild (ScrollView + custom fields), and keyboard/focus behavior needs a device pass.
  • Hangar bar glyph. The custom Hangar glyph and the Leaders SF Symbol differ in optical weight. The fix would swap the custom glyph for an SF Symbol, which is a brand call.
  • "1ST" badge instead of the sparkle. The first-of-type sparkle disc reads a bit generic. A mono "1ST" chip in ledger gold would match the ledger's FIRST OF TYPE line.
  • Results verdict for non-winners. "3rd of 4" in display type repeats the header's place. A quieter "710 points behind the winner" line was proposed; it's a copy call.
  • IATA vs ICAO across surfaces. The same route shows IATA on one surface and ICAO on another. Needs a data decision, not a style one.

Reverted after the visual check

  • DIST as a third stat column on routeless cards. It reversed the deliberate "never a cramped third column" call and made the reveal shrink when a routeless catch finished saving (the 2026-10-26 no-jump fix).
  • Top-anchored restore screens with a 170 pt icon slot. It left a big dead gap under the small sweep and wifi icons.
  • A wider gap above "About this plane". Even 4 extra points pushed the 6.1" reveal into scrolling (RevealShortScreenTests).
